approvedHook: You deleted the leaked API key. Why can it still work?
approvedCta: Check which exposed credentials still need revoking.
narration: You deleted the leaked API key. Why can it still work?
Removing a key from a document changes that document. It does not automatically invalidate the credential at its provider.
This is a local teaching simulation with a dummy token. No real account or production credential is involved.
The simulated request succeeds before removal. It still succeeds after the document copy is cleared, because the registry still accepts it.
When the simulation revokes the token in that registry, the same request is denied. Removal and revocation are different actions.
For an actual exposure, follow the provider instructions to revoke or rotate the credential. GitHub recommends doing that first.
Update authorized services that need a replacement, then check that they work and the exposed credential no longer grants access.
Review the affected logs and copies without pasting the secret into another chat or screenshot.
This demonstration explains the boundary. It does not prove a real incident is resolved or test your provider.
Check which exposed credentials still need revoking.
